paragraphs.source_en: 2 (p. 278) dissolved into the earth: While Heathcliff’s opening of Catherine’s grave certainly smacks of Gothic fiction, the preservation of her body after eighteen years is not far-fetched, since peat in the soil in the area around Haworth had precisely this effect. In chapter 3, Lockwood refers to this fact when he describes a chapel that is “near a swamp, whose peaty moisture is said to answer all the purposes of embalming on the few corpses deposited there.”
